transcript.heading: News Report One (American Male)
paras: A new community college program in Texas is offering free tuition to all graduates of the state's public high schools. The program, called Texas Promise, will cover the full cost of tuition and fees for any student who graduates with a minimum 2.0 GPA and completes community service hours. Officials estimate the program will help over 100,000 students attend college each year who otherwise might not be able to afford higher education. The program is funded through a combination of state appropriations and private donations from local businesses and philanthropic organizations. Texas joins a growing number of states that have implemented similar free college programs in an effort to increase educational attainment and strengthen the local workforce. The program will begin accepting applications for the fall semester starting next month.

transcript.heading: News Report Two (British Female)
paras: Norway has opened the world's first tunnel specifically designed for ships, allowing vessels to pass through a narrow, dangerous stretch of coastline. The Stad Ship Tunnel cuts through a solid rock peninsula and measures 1.7 kilometers long, 37 meters high, and 26.5 meters wide. The tunnel can accommodate ships up to 16,000 tons, including cruise ships and cargo vessels. Before the tunnel opened, ships had to navigate around the Stadhavet Sea, one of the most dangerous areas along the Norwegian coast, where rough weather conditions often delayed or endangered vessels. Construction on the project began in 2017 and cost approximately $330 million. Officials expect the tunnel to improve safety, reduce travel times, and boost coastal tourism in the region.
Questions 4 and 5 are based on the news report you have just heard.

5. What problem did the tunnel solve?

transcript.heading: News Report Three (American Female)
paras: A major consumer electronics company has announced it will stop including chargers and earphones in the boxes of all its new smartphones starting next year. The company says the decision will reduce electronic waste by over 2 million tons annually by eliminating hundreds of millions of unused accessories. The company argues that most customers already have compatible chargers and earphones from previous devices. However, the move has faced criticism from some consumers who say they will now have to purchase these items separately at additional cost. Several other electronics manufacturers have already implemented similar policies in recent years. The company says the smaller packaging will also allow 70% more boxes to fit on shipping pallets, reducing carbon emissions from transportation.
Questions 6 and 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.
6. What will the company stop including in new smartphone boxes?

transcript.heading: Conversation One (British Female + British Male)
paras: Woman (Maria): Hi Alex, are you going to the international student orientation this afternoon?
Man (Alex): Yeah, I think so, Maria. I'm a little nervous about it, actually. This is my first semester studying abroad in the UK, and I'm not really sure what to expect.

Woman: Don't worry! I went last year when I first arrived from Spain. It's really helpful. They'll explain how to register for classes, set up a bank account, register with a doctor, all that practical stuff.
Man: That sounds exactly what I need. I still haven't figured out how to get a student ID card or where to buy textbooks.
Woman: They'll have people there to help with all of that. Also, it's a great way to meet other international students. I made most of my friends during orientation week last year.
Man: That's good to hear. Do you think I need to bring anything with me?
Woman: Just your passport and your acceptance letter, that's about it. They'll provide snacks and drinks too, so you don't even need to bring money.
Man: Where is it being held? I heard it was in the student union building, but I'm not sure which room.
Woman: It's in the main hall on the first floor. It starts at 2 PM, but I'd get there about 15 minutes early if I were you - it gets pretty crowded.
Man: Thanks so much, Maria. I feel much better about it now. Would you like to walk over together?
Woman: Sure! I'm actually going to help volunteer this year, so I need to be there early anyway. Let's meet at the main entrance of our dorm at 1:30.

Man: I'm sorry to hear that. We have a wide selection of washing machines. Are you looking for a top-loading or front-loading model?
Woman: I'm not really sure. What's the difference?
Man: Front-loading machines are generally more energy efficient and use less water, but they tend to be more expensive. Top-loaders are usually cheaper and faster, but they use more water and energy.

Man: Absolutely. This model here is a front-loader that's very popular. It has a 4.5-cubic-foot capacity, multiple wash cycles, and it's Energy Star certified. It's currently on sale for $699.
Woman: That's a bit more than I was hoping to spend. Do you offer financing?
Man: Yes, we offer 12-month interest-free financing if you qualify. We also include free delivery and installation, and a one-year warranty.

transcript.heading: Passage One (British Male)
paras: The English language has one of the largest vocabularies of any language in the world, with estimates of total word count ranging from 500,000 to over 1 million words. Interestingly, English has borrowed words from hundreds of other languages throughout its history. After the Norman Conquest of England in 1066, French became the language of the ruling class for nearly 300 years, which is why English has many pairs of words with similar meanings - one from Germanic origins (like "cow" or "swine") and one from French (like "beef" or "pork"). Latin has also had an enormous influence, especially in academic, legal, and religious vocabulary. In modern times, English continues to absorb words from languages around the world, including "shampoo" from Hindi, "pizza" from Italian, "sushi" from Japanese, "robot" from Czech, and "safari" from Swahili. New words are constantly being added to the language, particularly in fields like technology, science, and popular culture. The Oxford English Dictionary adds approximately 1,000 new words every year.

transcript.heading: Passage Two (American Female)
paras: Regular physical exercise is one of the most important things you can do for your health. The World Health Organization recommends that adults get at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity or 75 minutes of vigorous activity per week, along with muscle-strengthening exercises at least two days per week. The benefits of regular exercise are numerous and well-documented. Exercise helps control weight, reduces the risk of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, and certain cancers. It also strengthens bones and muscles, improves mental health and mood, enhances brain function and memory, and can even help you sleep better. Despite these benefits, physical inactivity remains a major global public health problem. The WHO estimates that one in four adults worldwide does not meet the recommended activity levels. Experts note that exercise doesn't have to mean going to a gym or playing organized sports. Activities like brisk walking, dancing, gardening, swimming, or climbing stairs all count towards your weekly activity goals. Even small changes, like taking the stairs instead of the elevator or going for a short walk after meals, can add up to significant health benefits over time.

transcript.heading: Passage Three (British Female)
paras: The development of the printing press by Johannes Gutenberg in the 1440s revolutionized the spread of knowledge and ideas in Europe and around the world. Before the printing press, books were copied by hand, a process that was extremely time-consuming and expensive. As a result, books were rare and precious items, accessible only to wealthy individuals, the Church, and universities. Gutenberg's invention used movable metal type, which allowed pages to be composed quickly and reproduced in large numbers. The first major book printed using this new technology was the Gutenberg Bible, completed around 1455. The printing press led to an explosion in book production: by 1500, there were printing presses in over 200 European cities, and more than 20 million books had been printed. This mass production of books helped fuel the Renaissance, the Protestant Reformation, and the Scientific Revolution by making information widely available at affordable prices. It also contributed to the standardization of languages and the spread of literacy. The printing press is often considered one of the most important inventions in human history, laying the groundwork for the modern knowledge-based economy.
